correctness.rationale: All p>q>=2 are handled by an unrestricted gap upper bound from symmetrization and PSD monotonicity, a 4x4 inertia calculation, an affine eigenvector Rayleigh comparison, the opposite-sign perturbation, and an independent Perron bound on negative transition eigenvalues. originality.rationale: General FMMC convex and symmetry principles are prior art; the candidate supplies a distinct all-parameter high-imbalance rational optimum and a quartic necessary-and-sufficient threshold. The 2009 clique-barbell result has equal cluster sizes and internal clique edge variables; the present graph is an unequal tree and the closed formulas are not a direct specialization. The nearest accessible comparison findings are about a Cartesian-product star network or fourth-order integrator positivity, not unequal-tree SLEM. Unindexed equivalent work is still possible.
residual_risks: FMMC is a classical semidefinite optimization problem; an unindexed graph-family specialization could reproduce the result.
A non-obvious reduction from a broader unequal-clique or tree spectral-optimization theorem outside inspected material could imply the formula.

value.rationale: A naturally selected two-bottleneck network family has a closed rational globally fastest-mixing policy exactly beyond a sharp imbalance threshold. The competing quotient and leaf-difference eigenvalues create a structural spectral transition, and the critical imbalance tends to 1+sqrt(2). The theorem gives an actionable graph-dependent allocation rule, not merely a fixed numerical example. The complementary regime remains unsolved.
